grading_method: Evaluator manually compared every requested material part of each answer with the fixed source-backed key and frozen summary; support labels did not determine grades. Key details not requested by question are not mandatory.

grades.question: How are Factory cards, encounter tokens, and the structure bonus set up, and who starts?
grades.expected_answer: Shuffle Factory cards; select players+1 face-down and return others unseen to box. Put an encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly select one face-up structure bonus tile. Lowest numbered Player Mat starts, then clockwise.
grades.observed_answer: Shuffle Factory cards and randomly select players + 1 face-down for the board; return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup: ‘number of players + 1’; ‘one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories’; ‘one structure bonus tile’; ‘The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.’
grades.reason: Factory selection/count/unseen return, 11 encounters, random face-up tile and lowest-mat starter resolved.

grades.question: What starts on the map and each mat, and which mat supplies starting power, combat cards, popularity, coins and objectives?
grades.expected_answer: Character on own home base; one worker on each of two land-adjoined territories. Faction Mat supplies power/combat cards, holds four mechs and six stars. Player Mat supplies popularity/coins/objectives, holds six technology cubes on black-square green boxes, four structures, four recruits and remaining six workers on Produce; action token starts beside it.
grades.observed_answer: At setup, place the character at home; two workers on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining home; four mechs over the Faction Mat abilities; six stars by the faction emblem; six technology cubes in the Player Mat green boxes marked with a black square; four structures in their matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits on its bottom-row circular spaces; the remaining six workers on its Produce red rectangles; and the action token beside the Player Mat. Leave the Faction Mat one-time recruit spaces empty. The Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; the Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins, and two objective cards.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup, items 3–4: ‘Use the Faction Mat to set starting power and combat-card draw’; ‘Use the Player Mat to set starting popularity, coins and objectives (two objective cards)’; the setup piece table lists the starting positions.
grades.reason: Map and mat pieces, action-token starting location and correct assignment of starting values resolved.

grades.question: May you skip both actions, repeat a section, use top-row gains below, or take the bottom action first? How are costs and benefits determined?
grades.expected_answer: Must move token to different section, except Rusviet may repeat including Factory. Top then bottom, each optional once; may skip both. May use top gains below. Pay full exposed red-box cost before taking as much or as little exposed green benefit as desired.
grades.observed_answer: You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action (a dead turn), either action, or both. If taking both, take the top before the bottom; you cannot return to the top afterward. Rusviet may repeat a section, including its Factory card. Top-row gains may pay bottom-row costs. Costs are all exposed red boxes and must be paid in full before the action; benefits are exposed green boxes and may be taken as much or as little as desired. Exact bottom-row resource costs and coin benefits depend on the Player Mat and upgrades.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: ‘different section’; ‘first pay the full cost’; ‘choose as much or as little’; ‘You may use top-row gains to pay the bottom-row cost’; ‘bottom first is not allowed’; ‘Rusviet may repeat a section.’
grades.reason: Mandatory token move, optional actions/ordering, Rusviet exception, top gains below, exposed full costs/optional gains resolved.

grades.question: Who controls a structure territory occupied by an enemy worker, who can use the structure, and from where may you spend resources for an action elsewhere?
grades.expected_answer: Enemy worker controls territory and resources; structure owner retains abilities except cannot Produce at an uncontrolled Mill; enemy gains no structure ability. Spend resources from any controlled territories for actions anywhere; spent resources go to supply.
grades.observed_answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls the territory and all its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you keep those abilities even without control, except a Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. You may pay action costs with resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
grades.reader_evidence: Control, resources and home bases: ‘An enemy worker alone on your structure’s territory controls it and all its resources’; ‘Enemy units do not gain your structure’s abilities’; ‘Pay costs using resources from any territories you currently control, even to act elsewhere.’
grades.reason: Enemy worker control, owner-only persistent structure ability/Mill exception and remote resource spending resolved.

grades.question: On a normal unupgraded Move, can one unit move twice, can a transported worker subsequently move, and who can carry what?
grades.expected_answer: Move up to two different units one adjacent territory each, sequentially, or gain $1 instead. All units carry any number of resources; only mechs carry any number of own workers, not characters. Carriage is not the worker movement so worker can subsequently move itself.
grades.observed_answer: No. On the normal Move, you may move up to two different units one adjacent territory each; you cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice. Mechs can carry any number of your workers (never your character); all units can carry resources. A transported worker's carried movement does not count as its own, so it may subsequently move itself, or may move onto a mech and be carried by that mech's later move.
grades.reader_evidence: Move OR coins: ‘move up to two different units’; ‘cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice’; ‘Only mechs may also carry any number of your workers’; ‘Being carried does not count as the worker’s own movement.’
grades.reason: Distinct-unit movement, transported worker own movement and all resource/mech worker transport restrictions resolved.

grades.question: What happens when a Speed-enabled mech enters enemy workers only, even at zero popularity; may its workers enter that territory by themselves?
grades.expected_answer: Mech stops and cannot move again this turn. Enemy workers immediately retreat home leaving resources; attacker loses one popularity each to minimum zero, still retreats them. Workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
grades.observed_answer: A character or mech entering a territory with only enemy workers stops and cannot move again that turn. Those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources; lose one popularity per worker, down to zero. Insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat. It is not combat. The mech's own workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
grades.reader_evidence: Move OR coins: ‘Your character/mech entering enemy workers only stops’; workers ‘immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources’; ‘Lose one popularity per worker, down to zero’; ‘A worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.’
grades.reason: Enemy-worker-only stop, immediate home retreat/resources, popularity floor and independent worker-entry restriction resolved.

grades.question: When does combat occur after movement, who chooses multiple combat order, and can workers enter or leave enemy-character/mech-controlled territory alone?
grades.expected_answer: Finish all movement, then combats before bottom-row action. Active attacker chooses order. Attacking plastic unit stops on entry and enemy temporarily controls territory. Workers cannot enter or leave such territory independently.
grades.observed_answer: After the attacker finishes moving the other units, resolve all combat before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
grades.reader_evidence: Move OR coins: ‘Finish moving the other units, then resolve all combats before the bottom-row action; attacker chooses multiple-combat order’; a worker cannot independently move ‘into or out of’ territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
grades.reason: Combat after all movement/before bottom, attacker ordering and independent worker enter/leave prohibition resolved.

grades.question: State Bolster and Trade costs and choices; where are traded resources placed and what if all workers are home? What if the combat deck is exhausted?
grades.expected_answer: Bolster $1 for 2 power OR 1 combat card; Trade $1 for any two resources OR 1 popularity. Place resources on controlled territory with worker; cannot trade for resources with all workers home. Empty combat deck reshuffles discards; if both empty draw none.
grades.observed_answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card before upgrades. If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discard pile are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources, same or different, or one popularity, before upgrades. Traded resources go on a controlled territory with at least one worker. You cannot Trade for resources if all your workers are at home. A built Monument adds one popularity to Bolster; a built Armory adds one power to Trade.
grades.reader_evidence: Bolster: ‘Pay $1, gain two power OR one combat card’; empty deck reshuffle and both-empty rule. Trade: ‘Pay $1’; resources go to ‘a controlled territory containing at least one worker’; ‘cannot Trade for resources if all your workers are at home.’
grades.reason: Both $1 top-action choices, worker-controlled trade placement/home prohibition and deck exhaustion branches resolved.

grades.question: How is Produce paid and resolved, where do new workers come from, can benefits be declined, and do new workers change the cost already paid?
grades.expected_answer: Pay all exposed red costs before action, must afford full power/popularity/coins. Choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker may produce one terrain token there. Villages produce workers from Player Mat left to right, after payment, so new exposure affects future Produce costs. May decline production/workers. Workers never return to mat.
grades.observed_answer: Produce first requires paying every exposed Produce cost in full, including power, popularity and/or coins, before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that same territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and are put in the producing village after payment. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Exposing new costs affects future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
grades.reader_evidence: Produce steps: ‘Pay every exposed Produce cost … in full before production’; ‘Each worker … may produce one’; ‘Take new workers from the Player Mat left to right, after payment’; ‘You may decline’; new costs affect ‘future Produce actions.’
grades.reason: Full exposed pre-payment, terrain production, left-to-right village workers, optional benefits and future-cost timing resolved.

grades.question: What are Upgrade and Deploy costs, placement restrictions and effects, and can a completed bottom action still be paid?
grades.expected_answer: Upgrade oil: cube from any green box to empty bracketed red box, never solid border. Deploy metal: choose mech on Faction Mat, put on controlled worker territory, never lake; uncovered ability applies to character/all mechs, not workers. Costs/coins vary by mat. Completed bottom action may still be paid for coins and applicable recruit bonus.
grades.observed_answer: Upgrade costs oil: move any technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost; solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy costs metal: put a chosen mech on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability applies from then on to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after all upgrades, mechs, structures, and recruits are completed, you may still pay for the bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
grades.reader_evidence: Bottom-row actions: ‘Upgrade — oil’; ‘Deploy — metal’; ‘The uncovered ability applies from now on to your character and every mech, not workers’; completed actions may still be paid for coins and recruit bonuses.
grades.reason: Missing rule for required variable resource amount: pay the exposed Player Mat cost, varying with mat/upgrades. Earlier resource-only acceptance was too lenient under the unchanged question/key. See grading-correction.json.

grades.question: Where may a structure be built, can it move or be destroyed, and how do Mill and Mine work when their territories are occupied by enemies?
grades.expected_answer: Build costs wood, controlled worker territory, one structure total per territory; Factory allowed, lakes/home bases forbidden. Permanent cannot move/destroy. Mill adds bonus Produce territory and produces as worker plus actual workers only while controlled. Mine personal tunnel usable for all unit movement even enemy-controlled, enemy cannot use it.
grades.observed_answer: Build costs wood. Place a structure on a controlled territory with your worker; only one structure total may be on a territory, including opponents' structures. The Factory is allowed; lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot be moved or destroyed. A Mill supplies a bonus Produce territory and produces as one worker only while you control its territory; an enemy unit there removes control, so the Mill cannot produce. A Mine is your personal tunnel for all your unit movement, including Factory Move, even while enemy-controlled; it does not grant opponents its ability.
grades.reader_evidence: Build: ‘controlled territory with your worker’; ‘Only one structure total’; ‘Structures cannot be moved or destroyed’; Mill works ‘only while controlled’; Mine is ‘personal tunnel … even when enemy-controlled.’
grades.reason: Worker/control structure placement, single-structure/terrain restrictions, permanence and enemy-control Mill/Mine exceptions resolved.

grades.question: When enlisting, where does the token go, what are the one-time bonuses, which action sets ongoing bonus, and how do simultaneous/two-player bonuses resolve?
grades.expected_answer: Pay food; remove any recruit from Player Mat, permanently place on open Faction one-time space for 2 power/coins/popularity/combat cards. Ongoing bonus linked to section uncovered, triggered by self or immediate left/right taking that bottom action, not top/Factory. Announce actions. Active then left then right; sixth star immediately ends. In 2-player opponent triggers once.
grades.observed_answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row section of your Player Mat and put it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat. Immediately gain the chosen one-time bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is determined by the Player Mat circle uncovered where the recruit was removed: Upgrade gives one power, Deploy one coin, Build one popularity, Enlist one combat card. For a triggered bonus, resolve active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play, the opponent triggers it once, not twice.
grades.reader_evidence: Enlist: recruit from ‘any bottom-row section’; one-time bonus list. Ongoing recruits: bonus is the ‘circle uncovered where you removed the recruit’; resolve ‘active player first, then left, then right’; two-player opponent triggers ‘once, not twice.’
grades.reason: Permanent open Faction placement, four one-time choices, uncovered-section ongoing trigger, active-left-right and two-player exception resolved.

grades.question: What may each combatant secretly spend on dial and cards, how do combat abilities resolve, and how are totals paid and ties broken?
grades.expected_answer: May fight at zero power/popularity. Attacker mech ability first, then defender. Dial 0 to min(current power,7). Up to one card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial. Reveal simultaneously; add card values, attacker wins tie. Both pay dial power and discard used cards face-up; card values do not reduce track.
grades.observed_answer: Each player secretly chooses dial power from 0 to the smaller of seven and current power. They may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial power; Rusviet People's Army adds one additional card total if any workers are present. Workers alone never fight. If both combatants have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial and card values; attacker wins ties. Each player, winner and loser alike, deducts their dial power from the power track and discards every played card face-up. Card values do not deduct extra track power.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat steps 1–3: dial ‘0 to the smaller of seven and your current power’; cards per participating character/mech; ability order attacker then defender; ‘attacker wins ties’; both players deduct dial and discard cards.
grades.reason: Capped dial/card spending, attacker-first abilities, simultaneous reveal/tie, both dial payments and used-card face-up discard resolved.

grades.question: After combat, what happens to all units/resources, popularity, combat stars, and the losing player combat-card reward?
grades.expected_answer: Winner controls territory/resources, places combat star if below two (Saxony unlimited available stars), may still fight after limit. Loser retreats all units including workers home leaving resources. Winning attacker loses one popularity per opposing worker retreated; winning defender does not. Loser draws one combat card if revealed at least one power on dial OR cards, none for zero total.
grades.observed_answer: The winner controls the territory and resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally at most two combat stars; Saxony has no usual limit within six available). All losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy allows eligible units and carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, even workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none. Polania Camaraderie exempts the specified post-combat aggressor worker retreat loss. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat step 4 covers territory, stars, retreats and resources; step 5 covers attacker popularity loss and loser card draw.
grades.reason: Winner control/star limit, all-unit retreat/resources, attacker/defender popularity and dial-or-card loser reward resolved.

grades.question: When is an encounter resolved after contested entry, what if the character loses, where do gains go, and do normal action costs/bonuses apply?
grades.expected_answer: Character stops/cannot move again on entering token; finish Move and all combats before bottom action, only if character still there (must win contested entry). If loses token stays. Discard token, draw encounter, choose one affordable option (Polania up to two); pay printed cost and may decline benefits. Resources/structures/mechs/workers go to encounter territory. No additional normal costs/benefits or recruit bonuses; card face-down bottom encounter deck.
grades.observed_answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter only if the character remains in the territory; discard the token and draw the card before a following bottom action. If the character loses contested entry, it retreats and the encounter token stays. All resources, workers, mechs, and structures gained go to the encounter territory. Pay no additional normal action costs and receive no additional mat benefits, including no ongoing recruit bonuses.
grades.reader_evidence: Encounters: ‘After the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there’; on lost contested entry ‘the token stays’; gains go to ‘the encounter territory’; ‘Pay no additional normal action costs’ or mat benefits/recruit bonuses.
grades.reason: After-Move/all-combat encounter eligibility, losing-character token persistence, benefit destination and isolated costs/bonuses resolved.

grades.question: Who takes a Factory card, when, may later visitors take one or change theirs, and how do Factory actions and Speed movement differ from mat actions?
grades.expected_answer: Each character first finishing Move at Factory after any combat must choose one available card, return rest; not just first visitor, max one permanent card per player, cannot exchange. Fifth section, optional top then bottom; no corresponding mat coins/structure/recruit bonuses. Bottom Move one unit up to twice (three with character/mech Speed), same stop rules, Mine usable.
grades.observed_answer: Every player's character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if necessary), looks at available Factory cards, chooses one, and returns the rest. Each player gets at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. The card acts as a fifth action section, with optional top then bottom under the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception). Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories within that Move action, or three for a character/mech with Speed; Mine access and ordinary movement/stop restrictions apply.
grades.reader_evidence: Factory: ‘Every player’s character’ on ‘its first finish of a Move action’; ‘one permanent card’; fifth section; no mat/recruit bonuses; bottom action moves one unit two territories, or three with Speed.
grades.reason: Every character first-visit eligibility, after-Move choice, one permanent card, independent Factory bonuses and Speed/normal movement resolved.

grades.question: When can an objective be revealed, what requirements and discards apply, and what changes for Saxony?
grades.expected_answer: Only own turn before/after complete top or bottom action, all requirements true at reveal; may delay reveal. Place one objective star, discard both objectives to deck bottom. Saxony keeps second and may complete both, unrestricted combat/objective stars within six available.
grades.observed_answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective; you may wait but must meet all requirements at the moment of reveal. Place its star and put both objective cards on the bottom of the deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed. Saxony retains the other card after the first objective and can score both.
grades.reader_evidence: Objectives and agreements: ‘Only on your own turn’; ‘meet all requirements at the moment of reveal’; put ‘both objective cards on the bottom’; Saxony retains the other card and can score both.
grades.reason: Own-turn complete-action timing, all requirements at reveal, deck-bottom discards and Saxony keep/score second resolved; specific card text was not requested.

grades.question: Which achievements earn stars, may stars be lost or another player block a goal, and when does the game end?
grades.expected_answer: Six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, eight workers on board, completed objective, up to two combat victories, 18 popularity,16 power. Must place on achievement, each once except combat two/Saxony exception; irreversible and other players may share goals. Sixth star ends immediately, no extra turns/actions.
grades.observed_answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. Stars are permanent if power or popularity later drops, and another player's stars never block a goal. Play ends immediately when someone places their sixth star.
grades.reader_evidence: Stars and immediate end: lists each achievement; ‘A placed star is permanent’; ‘Other players’ stars never block a goal’; ‘sixth star immediately ends play.’
grades.reason: All star achievements, permanence, shared goals and immediate sixth-star termination resolved.

grades.question: If a bottom action earns the sixth star, what is collected first; what happens to pending battles and a neighbor recruit star?
grades.expected_answer: Gain primary benefit, coins and own recruit ongoing benefit before placing bottom-action sixth star. Undo movement into any still-unresolved battle, return units to origin. Neighbor power/popularity star from recruit only after active action, in order active/left/right (clockwise), only if active did not already end game; stop remaining events at sixth star.
grades.observed_answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect the primary benefit, coins, and the active player's ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. Resolve neighbor power/popularity recruit stars in this order: finish the active action, active player first, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for a sixth star at each step; if an earlier player places the sixth star, later recruit stars or bonuses do not resolve. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement and return initiating units to their origin territories; do not resolve another combat.
grades.reader_evidence: Sixth-star sequence: collect ‘primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing that star’; neighbor order active, left, right; pending battle movement is undone and no other combat resolves.
grades.reason: Pre-star bottom benefits, pending-battle rollback and neighbor recruit priority/interruption resolved.

grades.question: At 10 popularity, how much do 5 stars, 4 normal territories plus Factory, and 13 resources add to held coins? Include structure bonus eligibility and all victory tiebreakers.
grades.expected_answer: Tier 7-12 pays $4/star,$3/territory,$2/resource pair. 5 stars=$20; 4+Factory as 3=7 territories=$21; six pairs=$12, total $53 plus held coins and structure tile. Structure bonus even without control. Most coins wins; ties workers+mechs+structures (not character), power, popularity, controlled resources, controlled territories, placed stars.
grades.observed_answer: At 10 popularity, each star is $4, each controlled territory $3, and each complete pair of controlled resources $2. Thus 5 stars = $20; four ordinary territories plus the Factory count as seven territories, scoring $21; 13 resources make six complete pairs, scoring $12. These add $53 to held coins. The selected structure bonus is also scored even if enemies control the player's structure territories. Tiebreakers, in order: workers + mechs + structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, stars placed.
grades.reader_evidence: Final fortune table/example gives at 10 popularity five stars, four ordinary territories plus Factory, and 13 resources = ‘$20 + $21 + $12 = $53’; structure bonus applies even if enemies control those territories; tiebreak sequence is listed.
grades.reason: Tier-2 rates, Factory as three, floor pairs and $53, retained coins/structure eligibility and exact tiebreak order resolved.

grades.question: When does combat occur after movement, who chooses multiple combat order, and can workers enter or leave enemy-character/mech-controlled territory alone?
grades.expected_answer: Finish all movement, then combats before bottom-row action. Active attacker chooses order. Attacking plastic unit stops on entry and enemy temporarily controls territory. Workers cannot enter or leave such territory independently.
grades.observed_answer: After all units finish moving in the Move action, resolve combats between opposing characters/mechs sharing a territory, before any following bottom-row action. The attacker chooses the order when there are multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat: “After all units finish a Move action ... fight, before any subsequent bottom action. The attacker chooses the order”; movement rules prohibit workers moving independently “into or out of” enemy character/mech-controlled territory.
grades.reason: Combat after all movement/before bottom, attacker ordering and independent worker enter/leave prohibition resolved.

grades.question: State Bolster and Trade costs and choices; where are traded resources placed and what if all workers are home? What if the combat deck is exhausted?
grades.expected_answer: Bolster $1 for 2 power OR 1 combat card; Trade $1 for any two resources OR 1 popularity. Place resources on controlled territory with worker; cannot trade for resources with all workers home. Empty combat deck reshuffles discards; if both empty draw none.
grades.observed_answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card (before upgrades). If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discard pile are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources, same or different, or one popularity (before upgrades). Traded resources go on a controlled territory containing at least one worker. You cannot Trade for resources if all your workers are at home.
grades.reader_evidence: Bolster: “Pay $1, gain two power OR one combat card”; empty-deck rule. Trade: “Pay $1”; resources go “on a controlled territory containing at least one worker”; cannot Trade for resources if all workers are home.
grades.reason: Both $1 top-action choices, worker-controlled trade placement/home prohibition and deck exhaustion branches resolved.

grades.question: How is Produce paid and resolved, where do new workers come from, can benefits be declined, and do new workers change the cost already paid?
grades.expected_answer: Pay all exposed red costs before action, must afford full power/popularity/coins. Choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker may produce one terrain token there. Villages produce workers from Player Mat left to right, after payment, so new exposure affects future Produce costs. May decline production/workers. Workers never return to mat.
grades.observed_answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost in full before production; the costs can be power, popularity and/or coins. Then choose up to two different controlled territories. Each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that same territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right after payment and are placed in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Workers newly exposed on the mat affect future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
grades.reader_evidence: Produce: “Pay every exposed Produce cost ... in full before production”; “Take new workers from the Player Mat left to right, after payment”; “Exposing new costs affects future Produce actions, not the cost already paid”; “You may decline some or all production.”
grades.reason: Full exposed pre-payment, terrain production, left-to-right village workers, optional benefits and future-cost timing resolved.

grades.question: What are Upgrade and Deploy costs, placement restrictions and effects, and can a completed bottom action still be paid?
grades.expected_answer: Upgrade oil: cube from any green box to empty bracketed red box, never solid border. Deploy metal: choose mech on Faction Mat, put on controlled worker territory, never lake; uncovered ability applies to character/all mechs, not workers. Costs/coins vary by mat. Completed bottom action may still be paid for coins and applicable recruit bonus.
grades.observed_answer: Upgrade costs oil: move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box on the Player Mat; this improves a top benefit and reduces a bottom cost. Solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy costs metal: place a chosen mech from the Faction Mat on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability applies from then on to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades, mechs, structures and recruits, you may still pay for a bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
grades.reader_evidence: Bottom-row actions: “Upgrade — oil”; “Deploy — metal”; mech placement and ability effects; “Even after completing all ... you may still pay for that bottom action.”
grades.reason: Missing rule for required variable resource amount: pay the exposed Player Mat cost, varying with mat/upgrades. Earlier resource-only acceptance was too lenient under the unchanged question/key. See grading-correction.json.

grades.question: Where may a structure be built, can it move or be destroyed, and how do Mill and Mine work when their territories are occupied by enemies?
grades.expected_answer: Build costs wood, controlled worker territory, one structure total per territory; Factory allowed, lakes/home bases forbidden. Permanent cannot move/destroy. Mill adds bonus Produce territory and produces as worker plus actual workers only while controlled. Mine personal tunnel usable for all unit movement even enemy-controlled, enemy cannot use it.
grades.observed_answer: Build by paying wood and place a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker. Only one structure total may be on a territory, including opponents' structures; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A Mill gives an extra Produce territory and produces as one worker, but only while you control its territory; it can produce without an actual worker there. Your Mine is a personal tunnel for all your unit movement, including Factory Move, and can be used even when enemy units occupy its territory. Opponents cannot use your building abilities.
grades.reader_evidence: Build: “controlled territory with your worker”; “Structures cannot be moved or destroyed”; Mill bonus applies “only while controlled”; Mine is a personal tunnel “even when enemy-controlled.”
grades.reason: Worker/control structure placement, single-structure/terrain restrictions, permanence and enemy-control Mill/Mine exceptions resolved.

grades.question: When enlisting, where does the token go, what are the one-time bonuses, which action sets ongoing bonus, and how do simultaneous/two-player bonuses resolve?
grades.expected_answer: Pay food; remove any recruit from Player Mat, permanently place on open Faction one-time space for 2 power/coins/popularity/combat cards. Ongoing bonus linked to section uncovered, triggered by self or immediate left/right taking that bottom action, not top/Factory. Announce actions. Active then left then right; sixth star immediately ends. In 2-player opponent triggers once.
grades.observed_answer: For Enlist, take a recruit from any bottom-row section of your Player Mat and place it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat. Immediately gain the selected one-time bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed, regardless of the one-time choice: Upgrade gives one power, Deploy one coin, Build one popularity, Enlist one combat card. When triggered by a bottom-row action, resolve active player first, then immediate left neighbor, then immediate right neighbor; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play, the opponent gets the bonus once, not twice.
grades.reader_evidence: Enlist: recruit from “any bottom-row section” to “any open one-time recruit bonus”; four one-time bonuses; ongoing bonus is “the circle uncovered where you removed the recruit.” Ongoing recruits specify active → left → right and two-player opponent triggers once.
grades.reason: Permanent open Faction placement, four one-time choices, uncovered-section ongoing trigger, active-left-right and two-player exception resolved.

grades.question: What may each combatant secretly spend on dial and cards, how do combat abilities resolve, and how are totals paid and ties broken?
grades.expected_answer: May fight at zero power/popularity. Attacker mech ability first, then defender. Dial 0 to min(current power,7). Up to one card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial. Reveal simultaneously; add card values, attacker wins tie. Both pay dial power and discard used cards face-up; card values do not reduce track.
grades.observed_answer: Each combatant secretly sets dial power from zero to the smaller of seven and current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, even at zero dial power. Rusviet People's Army adds one additional card total if any workers are present. If both players have combat mech abilities, the attacker uses theirs first, then the defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial plus card values; attacker wins ties. Each player loses the dial power they committed from their power track, and all played cards are discarded face-up; card values do not cost additional track power.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat steps 1–3: dial from “0 to the smaller of seven and your current power”; “one combat card per participating character/mech”; abilities “attacker uses theirs first, then defender”; attacker wins ties; dial payment and card discard.
grades.reason: Capped dial/card spending, attacker-first abilities, simultaneous reveal/tie, both dial payments and used-card face-up discard resolved.

grades.question: After combat, what happens to all units/resources, popularity, combat stars, and the losing player combat-card reward?
grades.expected_answer: Winner controls territory/resources, places combat star if below two (Saxony unlimited available stars), may still fight after limit. Loser retreats all units including workers home leaving resources. Winning attacker loses one popularity per opposing worker retreated; winning defender does not. Loser draws one combat card if revealed at least one power on dial OR cards, none for zero total.
grades.observed_answer: The winner controls the territory and its resources and places a combat star if eligible (ordinary limit of two combat stars; Saxony has no usual limit within the six available). All losing characters, mechs and workers retreat to their own home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy may instead retreat eligible units and carried workers onto adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat; a winning defender loses none, subject to Polania Camaraderie's stated exception. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat step 4: winner controls territory/resources and star eligibility; losing units retreat “leaving all resources”; step 5: attacker popularity loss and loser combat-card draw condition.
grades.reason: Winner control/star limit, all-unit retreat/resources, attacker/defender popularity and dial-or-card loser reward resolved.

grades.question: When is an encounter resolved after contested entry, what if the character loses, where do gains go, and do normal action costs/bonuses apply?
grades.expected_answer: Character stops/cannot move again on entering token; finish Move and all combats before bottom action, only if character still there (must win contested entry). If loses token stays. Discard token, draw encounter, choose one affordable option (Polania up to two); pay printed cost and may decline benefits. Resources/structures/mechs/workers go to encounter territory. No additional normal costs/benefits or recruit bonuses; card face-down bottom encounter deck.
grades.observed_answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on its token territory; then discard the token and draw a card before a following bottom action. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. Resources, workers, mechs and structures gained go to the encounter territory. Pay the encounter option's printed cost, but no additional normal action costs apply and no mat benefits, including ongoing recruit bonuses, are gained.
grades.reader_evidence: Encounters: “After the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there”; if entry is lost “the token stays”; gains go to “the encounter territory”; “Pay no additional normal action costs and gain no additional mat benefits.”
grades.reason: After-Move/all-combat encounter eligibility, losing-character token persistence, benefit destination and isolated costs/bonuses resolved.

grades.question: Who takes a Factory card, when, may later visitors take one or change theirs, and how do Factory actions and Speed movement differ from mat actions?
grades.expected_answer: Each character first finishing Move at Factory after any combat must choose one available card, return rest; not just first visitor, max one permanent card per player, cannot exchange. Fifth section, optional top then bottom; no corresponding mat coins/structure/recruit bonuses. Bottom Move one unit up to twice (three with character/mech Speed), same stop rules, Mine usable.
grades.observed_answer: Every player's character must take a Factory card on that player's first finish of a Move action at the Factory, after winning combat if needed. The player chooses one available card and returns the rest; this applies to each player, not only the first visitor. Each player gets at most one permanent card and later visits cannot exchange it. The card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom, subject to the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception). Similar Factory actions do not grant the corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses or ongoing recruit bonuses. The Factory card's bottom action moves one unit up to two territories during that Move action, or three for a character/mech with Speed; normal movement/stop restrictions and Mine access apply.
grades.reader_evidence: Factory: “Every player's character” takes a card on its “first finish of a Move action”; one permanent card, no later exchange; fifth action section; bottom action moves one unit up to two or three with Speed; no corresponding mat bonuses.
grades.reason: Every character first-visit eligibility, after-Move choice, one permanent card, independent Factory bonuses and Speed/normal movement resolved.

grades.question: When can an objective be revealed, what requirements and discards apply, and what changes for Saxony?
grades.expected_answer: Only own turn before/after complete top or bottom action, all requirements true at reveal; may delay reveal. Place one objective star, discard both objectives to deck bottom. Saxony keeps second and may complete both, unrestricted combat/objective stars within six available.
grades.observed_answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective. You may wait, but must meet all requirements at the moment of reveal. Place its star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed; Saxony retains the other card and can score both.
grades.reader_evidence: Objectives: “Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action”; meet “all requirements at the moment of reveal”; put “both objective cards on the bottom”; Saxony can score both.
grades.reason: Own-turn complete-action timing, all requirements at reveal, deck-bottom discards and Saxony keep/score second resolved; specific card text was not requested.

grades.question: Which achievements earn stars, may stars be lost or another player block a goal, and when does the game end?
grades.expected_answer: Six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, eight workers on board, completed objective, up to two combat victories, 18 popularity,16 power. Must place on achievement, each once except combat two/Saxony exception; irreversible and other players may share goals. Sixth star ends immediately, no extra turns/actions.
grades.observed_answer: A star is earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, a combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. Stars are permanent once placed even if power or popularity later drops. Other players' stars never block a goal. The game ends immediately when someone places their sixth star.
grades.reader_evidence: Stars and immediate end lists all nine achievements; says “Other players' stars never block a goal,” a placed star “is permanent,” and the sixth star “immediately ends play.”
grades.reason: All star achievements, permanence, shared goals and immediate sixth-star termination resolved.

grades.question: If a bottom action earns the sixth star, what is collected first; what happens to pending battles and a neighbor recruit star?
grades.expected_answer: Gain primary benefit, coins and own recruit ongoing benefit before placing bottom-action sixth star. Undo movement into any still-unresolved battle, return units to origin. Neighbor power/popularity star from recruit only after active action, in order active/left/right (clockwise), only if active did not already end game; stop remaining events at sixth star.
grades.observed_answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect the primary benefit, coins and the player's ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. For neighbor power/popularity recruit stars, finish the active action, resolve the active player first, then the left neighbor, then the right neighbor, checking for a sixth star at every step; if an earlier player ends the game, later recruit stars or bonuses do not resolve. If units are still intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement by returning the initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat.
grades.reader_evidence: Sixth star: collect “primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing that star”; recruit sequence active → left → right; pending battle movement is undone and no further combat resolved.
grades.reason: Pre-star bottom benefits, pending-battle rollback and neighbor recruit priority/interruption resolved.

grades.question: At 10 popularity, how much do 5 stars, 4 normal territories plus Factory, and 13 resources add to held coins? Include structure bonus eligibility and all victory tiebreakers.
grades.expected_answer: Tier 7-12 pays $4/star,$3/territory,$2/resource pair. 5 stars=$20; 4+Factory as 3=7 territories=$21; six pairs=$12, total $53 plus held coins and structure tile. Structure bonus even without control. Most coins wins; ties workers+mechs+structures (not character), power, popularity, controlled resources, controlled territories, placed stars.
grades.observed_answer: At 10 popularity, each star is $4, each controlled territory is $3, and each complete pair of controlled resources is $2. Five stars yield $20; four ordinary territories plus Factory count as seven territories total and yield $21; 13 resources make six complete pairs and yield $12. These add $53 to held coins, plus the selected structure bonus. You earn the selected structure bonus even if enemies control your structures' territories. The winner is the player with the most total coins; ties break by workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring table at popularity 7–12: $4 per star, $3 per territory, $2 per resource pair. Factory “counts as three territories total”; example gives $20 + $21 + $12 = $53. Structure bonus applies “even if enemies control your structures' territories”; tie-break list follows.
grades.reason: Tier-2 rates, Factory as three, floor pairs and $53, retained coins/structure eligibility and exact tiebreak order resolved.
